brief.greeting: Good morning. LLMs are getting self‑aware about their own mistakes while Linux is patching up its old bugs.

stories.headline: LLMs tested for epistemic humility
stories.body: **Measuring modesty in models:** Researchers propose a framework that grades LLM agents on how they handle contradictory evidence, using Identify, Solve, and Escalate dimensions. The tests reveal where models bluff and where they defer.
stories.why: Helps you trust model outputs when they admit uncertainty.

stories.headline: LLM‑BlockFE turns text into code
stories.body: **Feature engineering without runtime calls:** The new system converts long documents into executable programs offline, so inference runs without hitting the LLM again. It trims latency and cost for production pipelines.
stories.why: You can ship lighter services that still benefit from LLM insight.

stories.headline: Linux Thursday security roundup released
stories.body: **Dozens of packages get patched:** Kernel, glibc, Python and other core libraries were updated across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora and more. The fixes address both remote exploits and privilege‑escalation bugs.
stories.why: Keeping your build environment safe prevents surprise break‑ins during CI.

highlights.title: Accurate but Not Humble: Evaluating Epistemic Humility in LLM Agents under Knowledge Conflict
highlights.summary: Introduces an evaluation framework for LLM agents' epistemic humility, measuring how they handle contradictory evidence via Identify, Solve, and Escalate dimensions.
highlights.detail: The framework distinguishes controlled conflicts, where parametric knowledge opposes retrieved evidence, from natural conflicts arising during multi-step tasks. It assesses agents' willingness to revise answers, express uncertainty, or persist incorrectly. This moves beyond traditional task-success metrics toward nuanced behavioral analysis.

highlights.title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search
highlights.summary: Presents LLM-BlockFE, an offline feature engineering system that converts long text into executable programs, eliminating LLM calls during online inference.
highlights.detail: LLM-BlockFE builds feature programs by appending immutable code blocks and uses a downstream model to evaluate candidates. To avoid greedy search pitfalls, it adds a block-level rollback mechanism. This approach targets industrial risk-control settings where real-time performance and cost constraints limit continuous LLM usage.

related.title: A New Type of LLM on the Block: Decision-Making Models

highlights.title: OnTrack: Real-Time Monitoring and Intervention in LLM Agent Trajectories via Streaming Structure-Aware Optimal Transport
highlights.summary: OnTrack monitors LLM agent actions in real time, comparing steps to successful reference runs and issuing alerts or blocks within about a millisecond per step.
highlights.detail: The system works under three access levels: full reference access, intermediate access with only tool schemas, and no prior knowledge beyond the current step. It aims to reduce cost and safety risks without the latency of safeguard agents that intervene at every step. OnTrack provides immediate feedback rather than post-hoc analysis.

related.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution

How Oracle turns days of work into minutes with ChatGPT and Codex
items.summary: Oracle uses ChatGPT Work and Codex to convert specialist knowledge into repeatable workflows that cut tasks from days to minutes across recruiting, engineering, and operations.
items.detail: The integration automates knowledge capture and execution, allowing non‑technical staff to trigger AI‑driven actions. It demonstrates a shift toward AI‑augmented internal tooling rather than external product features.

items.title: Introducing the Anthropic Cyber Mission
items.summary: Anthropic announced the Cyber Mission initiative.
items.detail: The brief announcement provides no further details on scope, timeline, or technical focus, leaving the specifics of the mission unclear.

items.title: LegalOn halves Codex costs while maintaining development speed
items.summary: LegalOn reduced daily Codex usage costs by 65% while keeping development speed unchanged.
items.detail: The cost cut was achieved by matching tasks to specific Codex models (Astra, Sol, Luna) and managing budgets strategically, showing that model selection can drive significant savings without performance loss.

items.title: Pollo AI turns creative ideas into campaigns with OpenAI
items.summary: Pollo AI leverages GPT‑5.6, GPT‑6 Astra, and GPT‑Image‑2.5 to generate detailed images and cinematic video ads from creative concepts.
items.detail: The platform targets creators needing rapid visual content, combining large language and image models to produce both static and moving media, expanding AI‑generated advertising workflows.

related.title: Building advertising for the way people use AI

items.title: Security updates for Thursday
items.summary: Thursday security updates were released for multiple Linux distributions, covering dozens of packages such as kernel, glibc, and Python across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, and others.
items.detail: The updates address vulnerabilities in core system libraries and tools, requiring administrators to apply patches promptly to maintain system integrity.

items.title: [$] The [vx]swap showdown
items.summary: The kernel swap layer has seen major changes this year, but the persistent‑swap‑file slot tie remains unresolved, with two competing patches still under discussion.
items.detail: Both proposals aim to decouple swap cache slots from file space to improve resource efficiency, yet neither has reached merge readiness, highlighting ongoing debate in the kernel community.

items.title: [$] An update on Rust's project goals
items.summary: At Kangrejos 2026, Rust Foundation program manager Tomáš Šedovič explained the Rust project's goal process and how it supports Rust for Linux developers.
items.detail: Šedovič co-leads the goals team, which tracks, organizes, and amends project goals. The overview highlighted how Rust for Linux has shaped several current goals. Understanding this process helps contributors align their work with the project's priorities.

items.title: Belt File from Old Mixer and Junk Bin Parts
items.summary: Hackaday featured a belt file built from an old mixer, showcasing upcycled power‑tool creation.
items.detail: The maker, bluesyann, repurposes discarded mixer components into a functional sanding tool. The project demonstrates practical recycling and offers a low‑cost alternative to commercial belt files.

items.title: Digital Signage in the Browser With Just a Click
items.summary: A new browser‑based digital signage solution lets users display text with a single click, reducing manual setup.
items.detail: The tool runs entirely in the browser, eliminating the need for separate software installations. It targets quick deployments for presentations, kiosks, or simple information boards.

items.title: Introducing the Garlic-Powered Door and Window Sensor
items.summary: A garlic‑powered door and window sensor eliminates the need for chemical batteries or external power.
items.detail: The sensor harvests energy from garlic’s natural electrochemical properties, providing a self‑sustaining power source. This design aims to improve reliability and reduce maintenance for home security systems.

items.title: IAmTomShaw/f1-race-replay
items.summary: IAmTomShaw/f1-race-replay is an interactive Formula 1 race visualisation and data analysis tool written in Python.
items.detail: The repository offers scripts to parse race telemetry and render animated track maps. It serves both hobbyists and analysts interested in exploring F1 performance data.

items.title: facebook/rebalancer
items.summary: facebook/rebalancer provides a DSL and solver for complex assignment problems such as constrained ball‑into‑box tasks.
items.detail: Implemented in C++, the tool lets users define custom rules and computes feasible allocations. It is useful for scheduling, resource distribution, and combinatorial optimization scenarios.

items.title: open-source-parsers/jsoncpp
items.summary: jsoncpp is an open-source C++ library that provides a simple API for parsing and generating JSON data.
items.detail: The library supports both DOM-style and SAX-style parsing, making it suitable for a range of performance needs. It is header-only, which simplifies integration into existing C++ projects, and is licensed under the MIT license, allowing unrestricted commercial use.

items.title: CursorTouch/Windows-MCP
items.summary: CursorTouch/Windows-MCP implements an MCP server that enables remote computer usage on Windows machines.
items.detail: The server facilitates mouse, keyboard, and clipboard sharing over the network, allowing multiple clients to control a Windows host. It is written in Python and targets easy deployment in corporate or lab environments where centralized control is needed.

items.title: SethRobinson/Patchy
items.summary: Patchy is an open-source image editor that aims for Photoshop‑compatible PSD handling and workflow.
items.detail: Patchy provides layer support, adjustment layers, and basic filters while preserving PSD file fidelity, making it a lightweight alternative for users needing occasional Photoshop‑style edits without a commercial license. The project is written in C++ and distributed under an MIT‑compatible license.

items.title: TigerVNC/tigervnc
items.summary: TigerVNC offers a high‑performance, cross‑platform VNC client and server implementation.
items.detail: It supports modern encryption, multi‑monitor setups, and efficient encoding to reduce bandwidth usage. The codebase is actively maintained, targeting both Linux and Windows environments, and is released under the GPL license.
